sources.source: Football-related arrests, banning orders: 2025 to 2026 domestic season
sources.verified_fact: The 23 July 2026 official release records 1,963 football-related arrests and other police actions, 2,460 banning orders in force on 1 June 2026, and 1,644 matches with reported incidents. Unauthorised entry entered Schedule 1 on 22 March 2026 and new incident categories affect year-on-year interpretation.
sources.quality_effect: Adds event-safety context with reporting-period, legal-category and incident-definition guards; match reports and banning orders are not neighbourhood prevalence or parcel-level safety measurements.

sources.source: Hate crime, England and Wales, year ending March 2025
sources.verified_fact: The official release records 137,550 police-recorded hate crimes. Because the Metropolitan Police changed recording systems in February 2024, MPS data is excluded from year-on-year comparisons; excluding MPS, 115,990 offences represented a 2% increase.
sources.quality_effect: Adds hate-crime context while enforcing the MPS series break, under-reporting and police-recording limitations; recorded offences are not a complete prevalence estimate or exact parcel risk.

sources.source: Police misconduct, England and Wales: year ending 31 March 2025
sources.verified_fact: The 22 January 2026 official release covers finalised misconduct cases across 43 territorial forces and distinguishes public complaint allegations, internally raised conduct matters and recordable conduct matters. The series is Official Statistics in Development.
sources.quality_effect: Adds police-accountability process context with finalised-case, allegation-category and development-statistic guards; case volumes are not crime incidence, service quality rates or parcel safety.

sources.verified_fact: The accredited release reports 1.59 million people formally dealt with by the criminal justice system in 2025, 226,300 out-of-court resolutions, and 67,000 defendants remanded in custody at magistrates' courts. It states that recorded-crime levels are influenced by police activity and recording practice.
sources.quality_effect: Adds justice-system flow context while separating charges, prosecutions, disposals, remand and sentences from victimisation, local incidence or parcel-level threat.

sources.source: Criminal court statistics quarterly: January to March 2026
sources.verified_fact: The 25 June 2026 accredited release reports a magistrates' court open caseload just above 370,000, a Crown Court caseload around 80,000, and more than 22,000 Crown Court cases open for at least a year.
sources.quality_effect: Adds court-capacity and timeliness context; open cases, receipts and disposals measure justice-system workload rather than offence prevalence, conviction probability or parcel safety.

sources.source: Offender management statistics quarterly: October to December 2025
sources.authority: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.verified_fact: The accredited release reports a prison population of 87,342 on 31 March 2026, 14,349 licence recalls in October to December 2025 and 248,568 people under probation supervision at 31 December 2025. The bulletin notes that recall and early-release policy changes affect flows.
sources.quality_effect: Adds custody, recall and probation context with stock-flow, reference-date and policy-change guards; administrative caseloads are not local crime rates or parcel-level risk.

sources.verified_fact: The 9 July 2026 release evaluates Circles of Support and Accountability using 533 male adults who began support between 2005 and 2020. The service currently contains reoffending data through June 2024.
sources.quality_effect: Adds rehabilitation-evaluation context with programme-selection, matched-comparison, cohort-period and outcome-lag guards; a programme estimate cannot be generalised to local prevalence or parcel safety.
